## Review (Claude)

### Pfizer (PFE): post version 1, as written

```text
📅 Pfizer ($PFE) goes ex-dividend on Nov 6, 2026.

The 5.73% yield is higher than the 4.88% five-year average.

https://quantic.finance/stocks/PFE
```

- **Version 2**: don't post it. "near the bottom of its range" isn't in the facts, which have no 5-year low. It's also wrong: PFE traded in the low 20s in 2025, so 30.05 isn't near the bottom. The 👟 means nothing here, and "30.05" has no currency.
- **Version 3**: "trades 49.1% below" presents the Nov 3 price as current. Putting a price fall next to a higher yield, with no reason given, hints at "it's cheap". The figures are right (30.05 / 59.05).

**What the sources say**
- Pfizer's [Q4 2026 dividend release](https://www.pfizer.com/news/press-release/press-release-detail/pfizer-declares-fourth-quarter-2026-dividend) confirms $0.43 a quarter (1.72 a year), record date Nov 6, 2026, payable Dec 7, 2026. With T+1 settlement the ex-date is the record date, so "ex-dividend on Nov 6" is right.
- Price: [TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/pfizer-rose-nearly-21-in-2026-as-its-forward-p-e-climbed-from-about-9-to-11-times-heres-what-november-3-has-to-show) has a $30.03 close on Oct 23, which fits 30.05. The Nov 3 close itself is **not confirmed**. 1.72 / 30.05 = 5.72%, so the data's 5.73% rounds a little high, which doesn't matter.
- The 59.05 five-year high matches PFE's Dec 2021 monthly close, which is inside the window.

**Time-sensitive**
- The ex-date is Friday, so post today or tomorrow.
- Pfizer reported Q3 on Nov 3. If the price moved much on Nov 4, the 5.73% is out of date: check a quote first.

### Brown-Forman (BF-B): post version 2, edited

```text
📊 Brown-Forman yields 3.18%, nearly double its 5-year average of 1.65%.

💵 Most of that is the share price falling: the dividend has grown 5.5% a year over five years, far less than the yield rose.

https://quantic.finance/stocks/BF-B
```

**Edits**: I dropped "64.1% below its 5-year high", because the 80.66 high isn't confirmed (see below). I added the average (1.65%) so "nearly double" can be checked, and I stated the cause the data gives (`why_the_yield_is_high`) instead of only implying it. Because it's edited, leave version 2 unticked.

- **Version 1**: "only grown 5.5% a year" is editorializing. The reasoning is also off: 5.5% growth isn't why the yield is high. The 📅 has nothing to do with the text.
- **Version 3**: don't post it. **"The dividend has risen for 38 years" is wrong**: Brown-Forman says 42 (below). "1.11 times its 5-year average" is jargon to a reader.

**What the sources say**
- Brown-Forman's [Nov 19, 2025 release](https://www.brown-forman.com/article/brown-forman-increases-cash-dividend-42nd-consecutive-year-november-19-2025) gives the **42nd consecutive annual increase**, quarterly $0.2265 → $0.2310 (annual $0.924). At 28.98 that's a 3.19% yield, so the 3.18% is consistent.
- Price: [Digrin](https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/BF-B/price) shows 28.95 for Nov 2026 and [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BF-B) $28.04 on Oct 29. Both fit 28.98.
- 5-year high 80.66: **not confirmed**. In Digrin's real prices the highest month is May 2021 (80.36), more than five years before Nov 2026. Inside a Nov 2021–Nov 2026 window the high looks lower, around the mid-70s (estimated from the adjusted series). If so, "64.1% below" overstates the drop by a couple of points.
- No Nov 2026 increase announcement found yet. Brown-Forman usually announces in mid-to-late November, so the yield could change soon.

### For Quantic's data
- **BF-B `streak_years` 38, against the company's 42.** This is a streak that runs short, like the earlier Microsoft (15) and Realty Income (28) cases. The data's `dividend_history_starts` is 2014, so the 38 can't come from that history either. Where does it come from?
- **BF-B `goes_ex_dividend_in` lists five months** (March, June, September, November, December) for a quarterly payer. The Q4 ex-date drifts between late November and early December from year to year, and the list is a union over years. It should probably pick one month per payment.
- **BF-B `price_high_monthly_5y`** may include months older than five years (see above).
- **Left out, MAIN with a streak of 0**: Main Street has never cut its regular monthly dividend and raises it often. A 0 suggests the streak is computed on annual totals that include supplemental dividends. Worth checking. EVT and DMLP pay variable distributions, so 0 is plausible for them.
- The left-out list reads "a streak of 1 years": a plural on the agent's side, cosmetic.
